press_wire.title: FOREST SUPPORTS WORLD HEART DAY
press_wire.summary: Nottingham Forest is pleased to support World Heart Day (September 29), which unites global organisations in raising awareness of cardiovascular disease (CVD). Organised by the World Heart Federation, it aims to prevent millions of premature deaths linked to CVD by encouraging people to take care of their hearts and ensuring everybody makes heart health a priority. This year’s campaign continues the momentum of ‘Don’t Miss a Beat’, raising awareness of the hidden or unnoticed symptoms of heart disease, and urging people to stay active, while also being proactive about routine screenings and warning signs. Heart disease kills around one in three people, more than any other condition – often due to symptoms being missed or overlooked. It can affect anyone, regardless of their age, fitness or lifestyle. Most deaths related to CVD are caused by risk factors that can be prevented or managed, which means that by making small, consistent changes, people can significantly improve their heart health over time. Modifiable risks include poor diet, physical inactivity, tobacco use, high cholesterol and high blood pressure. With this in mind, we’re joining other organisations in encouraging people to move for 20 minutes each day in September. Whether that’s running, cycling, playing a sport, or even walking to the shops – it all counts. Press here to download the oﬀicial World Heart Day app and join the movement. You can track your physical activities, get instant advice, and keep your heart healthy every day.

press_wire.title: Game4Hope Set For Goodison Park As Legends Return To Grand Old Lady
press_wire.summary: Game4Hope will now take place at Goodison Park on Saturday 26 September, giving some of football’s biggest names – and a host of Everton and Liverpool favourite – the opportunity to return to one of the sport’s most iconic stadiums. The inaugural charity fixture, which will raise vital funds and awareness in the fight against homelessness, will see Tim Cahill’s star-studded Merseyside XI take on a Rest of the World XI captained by Brazilian great Rivaldo, with kick-off remaining at 4.45pm (BST). The move from Hill Dickinson Stadium to Goodison Park adds another special dimension to an event already bringing together an extraordinary collection of football legends, celebrities and music stars. >>>SECURE YOUR GAME4HOPE AT GOODISON PARK TICKETS NOW<<< For Everton, this includes former players like Cahill, Leighton Baines, Phil Jagielka, Gareth Barry, Louis Saha and Joleon Lescott, it provides the opportunity to once again step out at the Grand Old Lady and play in front of supporters at a ground where they created so many memories. Everton Giant Peter Reid and Liverpool legend John Barnes will jointly manage the Merseyside XI – bringing together two men synonymous with opposite sides of one of football’s great city rivalries. For Reid, Goodison was the setting for some of the defining moments of his career. A central figure in Everton’s great side of the 1980s, he helped the Club win the 1984 FA Cup, League Championships in 1985 and 1987 and the 1985 European Cup Winners’ Cup, and was at the heart of one of Goodison’s most celebrated nights as Everton defeated Bayern Munich on the way to European glory. Returning to Goodison will therefore bring Reid back to a stadium indelibly linked to the most successful period of his playing career. For Barnes, the memories are very different but no less significant. During a decade as one of Liverpool’s greatest players, Goodison was the setting for some memorable and fiercely-contested Merseyside derbies. Barnes scored four times against the Blues, including in the famous 4-4 draw at Goodison in 1991. Now, rather than standing on opposite sides of the city’s rivalry, Reid and Barnes will share the Goodison dugout and unite Everton and Liverpool greats for a cause bigger than football. And there will be a sense of history for two of the biggest names in the Rest of the World XI. Brazilian World Cup winners Rivaldo and Cafu will return to Goodison Park more than 30 years after Brazil visited the stadium during the 1995 Umbro Cup where they took on and beat Japan. They will be joined in the Rest of the World squad by a host of international stars, including Clarence Seedorf, Jaap Stam, Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink, Mustapha Hadji and Des Walker. The football will be just one part of a packed day of entertainment, with supporters also able to enjoy live music, celebrity appearances, family activities and entertainment throughout the day. Chart-topping artist Tinie Tempah will provide the half-time entertainment. A host of stars from the worlds of television, film and sport will also take part, including Tony Bellew, Roman Kemp, Molly McCann, James Nelson-Joyce, Big Zuu, Liam Smith and Still Ryan, alongside Ted Lasso actors Toheeb Jimoh and Moe Hashim, former boxing world champion Johnny Nelson and Gladiators star Nitro. At the heart of Game4Hope is an issue far bigger than football. The event will raise funds and awareness for Everton in the Community and Shelter, supporting their work with people experiencing, or at risk of, homelessness across Merseyside and beyond. Game4Hope will bring Blues, Reds and football supporters from across the region together for an afternoon of football and entertainment while using the power of the game to shine a spotlight on one of the most significant challenges facing communities across the country. EXISTING GAME4HOPE TICKET HOLDERS Supporters who have already purchased tickets or Premium packages for Game4Hope at Hill Dickinson Stadium do not need to take any action at this stage. Everton’s Fan Centre and Premium teams will contact all existing purchasers directly with further information about their revised ticketing and package arrangements for the event at Goodison Park. With Cahill, Rivaldo, Cafu, Seedorf and some of the most recognisable names from Everton and Liverpool’s recent history preparing to grace the Goodison turf – alongside live music, celebrity guests and entertainment for the whole family – supporters are encouraged to secure their place now to avoid disappointment. >>>SECURE YOUR GAME4HOPE TICKETS NOW<<<

press_wire.title: Pre-Man Utd Press Conference
press_wire.summary: Álvaro Arbeloa knows Fulham will need to maintain recent levels if we’re to get a positive result against Manchester United on Sunday. A goalless draw at Anfield, followed by progression in the Carabao Cup from a testing fixture, has lifted the mood at Motspur Park going into our final game before the international break. “It’s obviously important winning games,” Arbeloa acknowledged. “I think it's the most important thing, and we have been talking for the last two or three weeks how important winning games is, even when you are doing a lot of things very well, you need to get points. And after that victory against West Ham, I think it has been a good week for us. “And now we are preparing for the game against Man United, and we are still believing that we can beat them, if we do a very good match from the first minute, and we know that we have to play at our best level – same level that we saw at Anfield – and that's our target.” It’s been a less rosy week for United, who exited the Carabao Cup after squandering a two-goal lead, a result which came after a controversial defeat in the Manchester derby. But Arbeloa laughed off any notions that this could be a good time to face Michael Carrick’s men. “When I see the players that they have, you can see they can win the game in one second,” he stated. “[Marcus] Rashford, [Matheus] Cunha, Bruno [Fernandes], [Youri] Tielemans, even the full-backs, they like to go forward. “They have very talented and top players and, of course, they are Man United, so you know what it means, and like I said before, if we want to beat them – and we believe that we can beat them – we need to play at the very high level that we did at Anfield for 90 minutes. “And even doing that, we couldn't beat Liverpool, we couldn't beat Chelsea, and I think in both games, we did really well. So, we are facing one of the best teams in the world, we know that, and we need to be ready.” Asked what it would mean to get that first Premier League win at the weekend, Arbeloa replied: “I think it will be so important. Not for me – for my team, for my players. I think I am not the important one here. “Fulham is important, and I think our supporters deserve one victory against Man United. I know that is so difficult, and the last time that we beat them here at Craven Cottage was too many years ago, so we will give our best and try to give them a victory.”

press_wire.title: Fulham FC and Fulham Pier welcome PSS as Official Partner
press_wire.summary: Fulham Football Club and Fulham Pier are pleased to announce a new partnership with PSS, a leading provider of professional cleaning services, as Official Venue Cleaning Partner. PSS plays an important role in maintaining the highest standards across Fulham’s key venues, providing professional cleaning services at Craven Cottage, Fulham Pier and our training ground. With a strong focus on quality, consistency and attention to detail, PSS helps ensure these spaces are maintained to the highest standards for supporters, staff, players, guests and visitors throughout the year. As an Official Partner, PSS joins the Club’s network of partners, strengthening an established relationship and creating opportunities to develop connections across Fulham’s wider business community. The partnership also reflects PSS’s commitment to working alongside leading organisations and supporting the smooth day-to-day operation of high-profile sporting, hospitality, retail and corporate environments. Looking ahead, the partnership will continue to evolve beyond matchdays, with PSS playing an important role in supporting the Club’s extensive operations and maintaining the exceptional standards across its everyday venues. This includes Fulham Pier’s premium destinations such as Lighthouse Social, Constance and Sael Spa, where attention to detail, presentation and guest experience are central to the offering. PSS’s expertise will help ensure these premium environments consistently deliver the quality and standards expected by guests, supporters and visitors alike. Jon Don Carolis, Chief Revenue Officer at Fulham Football Club, commented: “It is with pleasure that we welcome PSS as a new Official Partner. Having demonstrated their expertise and commitment to maintaining the highest standards across our venues over the last few years, we are delighted to have strengthened our relationship and formally welcome PSS to our partner network.” Mike Jones, Managing Director for PSS said: “We are delighted to formalise our partnership with Fulham Football Club and Fulham Pier and to become an Official Venue Cleaning Partner. Having supported the Club and its venues for several years, this is a natural progression of a relationship built on trust and shared high standards. “Our teams take great pride in supporting the experience across Craven Cottage, Motspur Park and Fulham Pier, ensuring every environment is maintained to the standards expected by supporters, guests, staff and visitors. We look forward to building on this partnership and supporting Fulham’s continued growth and success.” Fulham supporters and the wider business community can expect to see PSS’s presence grow throughout the season, as both organisations continue to build on an established relationship and work together towards an ambitious and successful partnership.
